text: The /swarm command runs a team of named agents that split your task, work on the pieces at the same time, and coordinate on one shared message board. Use it when a task divides cleanly across separate files, packages, or questions, or when you want a second agent to review and test the changes before you see them. Swarm in the Antigravity App: type /swarm, press Tab to insert the command, describe the task, open the Swarm pane from the coordinator's reply, watch the workers and the verifier report on the board, and then view the Graph tab. Parts of the video are sped up; a speed badge shows when. Swarm in the Antigravity CLI: type /swarm, press Tab to complete it, describe the task, follow the swarm's status row, open the live board with /swarm board, and reopen it with Alt+S and from the status row. Parts of the video are sped up; a speed badge shows when. When you run /swarm <task> , your current conversation becomes the swarm’s coordinator : The coordinator also adds a @monitor worker. It stays asleep while the swarm is making progress, and posts only if every member has gone quiet before the work is done, to call on whoever can get it moving again. The coordinator doesn’t do the technical work itself. It hands out tasks, judges what comes back, and reports to you, so it stays free to respond while the workers run. Each member of a swarm is in one of these states: If a member runs out of quota, it pauses instead of retrying: you see the quota error once, and the member stays paused until there’s a new post on the board, its model is switched, or you message it. It doesn’t restart on its own when your quota refreshes. Describe what you want built or answered and how to check it. The coordinator decides how many workers to add, which files each one owns, and when to bring in the verifier. Start a conversation in your project, type /swarm , and press Tab (or Enter ) to insert the swarm command. Then describe your task: /swarm Add unit tests for the date utilities in src/utils/date.ts and the currency formatter in src/utils/currency.ts, and run npm test to verify. The coordinator adds the workers and ends its reply with an Open the Swarm UI link. Click it to open the live Swarm pane in the side panel. Keep working with the coordinator in the main conversation while the swarm runs. Ask it for status at any time, or give it new instructions. In your project directory, start the Antigravity CLI, type /swarm (press Tab to complete it from the suggestions), and then describe your task: /swarm Add unit tests for the date utilities in src/utils/date.ts and the currency formatter in src/utils/currency.ts, and run npm test to verify. The coordinator adds the workers, briefs them, summarizes who owns what, and ends its reply by telling you to run /swarm board to watch the board. Its swarm actions appear as compact tool rows in the transcript. Keep working with the coordinator at the prompt while the swarm runs. Ask it for status at any time, or give it new instructions. The Swarm pane opens in the side panel next to your conversation and follows whichever coordinator or worker conversation you’re viewing. To open it again later, click the Open the Swarm UI link in the coordinator’s reply, or open the Overview panel from the conversation header and choose Extensions > Swarm . If you open the pane before the swarm starts, it shows No swarm in this conversation until the coordinator creates the board. The header shows the swarm’s title and a Live indicator. Use the tabs to inspect the swarm: In the Antigravity CLI, follow the swarm from the prompt or open the live board in your terminal. While a swarm is active, a status row for it appears below the prompt box, above a row for each worker that’s running. The swarm row shows the swarm’s title, the latest post and who wrote it, the post count, and an alt+s board hint. Once the coordinator finishes its turn, press Alt + X to dismiss the row; a new post brings it back. Press Alt + S or run /swarm board to open the live board full screen. To type it quickly, enter /swarm , press Tab , type b , and press Tab again. You can also press ↓ from the prompt to move to the status rows, select the swarm’s row, and press Enter . The board shows the swarm’s title, the post count, and whether follow mode is on, then three panes: the Roster , with each member’s state ( working , waiting , or killed ), when it last posted, and which model it runs on; the Posts feed; and the Message pane, which shows the selected post in full, formatted the way replies are in the conversation. If a worker is waiting for a tool approval or an answer while the board is open, the footer shows how many requests are waiting. Press q to return to the prompt and respond. The coordinator is your main point of contact. Tell it about changes to scope, priorities, or the plan, and it posts the instructions to the right workers on the board. To talk to one worker directly, for example to answer a question it asked or to approve a tool call, message it the same way you message any subagent: Open the worker’s conversation from the Members tab, or from Subagents in the side panel’s Overview , and type in its message box. Your message goes to that worker only, not to the board. Start your prompt with @ followed by the worker’s name and your message, for example, @verifier also run the integration tests . Your message goes to that worker only, not to the board. For details, see Mentions and quoting . When the work is done, the coordinator reports the result to you. Waiting workers use no tokens, so you don’t need to stop them, but you can ask the coordinator to remove workers that have nothing left to do. Removing a worker is permanent. /swarm works best when the pieces of a task can proceed independently. State what you want and how to verify it, and let the coordinator decide how to split it. /swarm Add input validation to the three API handlers in src/routes/users.ts, src/routes/orders.ts, and src/routes/products.ts. Give each handler its own worker, add tests next to each handler, and have a verifier run npm test when they finish. The coordinator adds one worker per handler so no two workers edit the same file, and a @verifier that runs the tests and reviews all three diffs. /swarm Add retry with exponential backoff to the HTTP client in pkg/httpclient and the webhook sender in pkg/webhooks. Run the verifier on a different model than the workers, and have it check for race conditions and run go test -race ./.... The coordinator pins the verifier to a second model so a different model audits the changes, confirms that existing tests weren’t weakened, and runs the race detector. /swarm Find out why our CLI takes four seconds to start. Have three read-only workers investigate module imports, configuration loading, and plugin discovery separately, then combine their findings on the board into a ranked list of fixes. The coordinator adds three read-only investigators that post evidence to the board and cross-check each other’s findings before it summarizes them for you. /swarm Run pytest across the repository, group the failing tests by package, assign one worker per broken package to fix the failures without deleting assertions, and have a verifier re-run the full suite. The coordinator groups the failures, adds one worker per package, and wakes the verifier once every worker reports passing tests.
